Official German wage tax tables that give net pay directly for a stated gross wage DO NOT EXIST and cannot be obtained for tax year 2026, because they were abolished. Established from the primary instrument, not inferred. The Bundesministerium der Finanzen publishes only Programmablaeufe (machine-calculation programmes) for wage tax, plus calculators and informational modules. The 2026 BMF navigation, which I read, lists exactly four wage-tax sections and no table: 'FAKTORVERFAHREN', 'BERECHNUNG DER LOHNSTEUER', 'ERMITTLUNG DES ZU VERSTEUERNDEN JAHRESBETRAGS' and 'ARBEITSLOHNGRENZEN'. Under BERECHNUNG DER LOHNSTEUER the only years offered are calculators (2026, 2025, 2024 Dezember, 2024 bis November, 2023 ab Juli, 2023 bis Juni, 2022, 2021), and the 2026 entry is titled 'Lohn- und Einkommensteuerrechner: Eingabeformular 2026 Lohnsteuer'. Corroborated by a secondary publisher of German wage tax tables, which I fetched and read and which states the position directly: 'Fuer den Lohnsteuerabzug gab es bis 2003 amtliche Lohnsteuertabellen von der Finanzverwaltung. Es werden nur noch Programmablaeufe zur Berechnung der Lohnsteuer veroeffentlicht. Mit den Lohnsteuerrechnern koennen Sie die Lohnsteuer stufenlos berechnen. Dennoch werden weiterhin (nicht amtliche) Lohnsteuertabellen veroeffentlicht, weil sie uebersichtlich sind und ohne maschinelle Berechnung einfach ablesbar sind.' CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS CORPUS: the ideal German evidence tier, an official tax authority publishing a net-pay table, is permanently unavailable. A net figure can only be produced by running the authority's own calculator or by implementing its Programmablaufplan, which is what DE/020_net_monthly_income.json and DE/020b_net_monthly_income_academics.json do.

employment_rate_within_12_months.note: Germany publishes no official per-graduation employment rate. net_monthly_income.note: This figure describes gross (before-tax) income, not take-home pay. It was filed on the net topic and has been demoted rather than published, because break-even must compare money out against money that actually reaches the worker. Using gross here would roughly halve the reported months in most European countries.

sources.notes: CONFIRMED from the primary federal statute, published by the Bundesamt für Justiz. Post-study job search in Germany: 18 MONTHS. Lawful name of the instrument: this is a residence permit ('Aufenthaltserlaubnis') granted under § 20 AufenthG for the purpose of 'Arbeitsplatzsuche im Anschluss an Aufenthalte im Bundesgebiet' (job search following residence in Germany). Germany does not use a named permit such as the UK's 'Graduate visa' or the Netherlands' 'orientation year'; the correct official naming for the corpus is a § 20 AufenthG Aufenthaltserlaubnis for job search (Arbeitsplatzsuche). Note precisely who the 18 months applies to: § 20(1) no. 1 covers students who successfully completed a study in Germany under § 16b or § 16c; numbers 1 to 4 share the 18-month cap. Number 5 (care/nursing Assistenz- or Helferausbildung) gets 12 months extendable once by 6. IMPORTANT CONDITION: securing livelihood (Lebensunterhaltssicherung) is a precondition, and extension beyond these periods is expressly excluded. I initially fetched § 27 AufenthG expecting the study/job-search provision and it turned out to be family reunification — recorded here so the corpus does not cite § 27 for this purpose.

sources.notes: CONFIRMED from the primary federal statute. Germany permanent residence: minimum 5 YEARS of holding an Aufenthaltserlaubnis (§ 9(2) sentence 1 no. 1). Official name: Niederlassungserlaubnis, which per § 9(1) is an UNLIMITED-STAY residence title (unbefristeter Aufenthaltstitel). IMPORTANT CAVEAT THAT MATTERS FOR A SCHOLARSHIP CORPUS: § 9(4) no. 3 provides that lawful residence for the PURPOSE OF STUDY OR VOCATIONAL TRAINING in Germany counts only HALF ('zur Hälfte'). So a period spent on a student residence permit does NOT count 1:1 toward the 5 years for permanent residence — it counts at half. A corpus entry of '5 years' must carry this halving rule or it is misleading. Additional requirements confirmed: livelihood secured, 60 months of pension contributions, adequate German language skills (B1 per § 2(11) AufenthG), basic knowledge of German law and society, sufficient living space. A separate 3-year route exists only for spouses of holders of a Niederlassungserlaubnis under § 18c (mobile employment) — NOT a general rule and not applicable to ordinary graduates, so it is recorded but explicitly flagged as inapplicable. Halving of study periods also applies, so the practical time to Niederlassungserlaubnis for a graduate who studied the whole period in Germany is substantially longer than 5 calendar years.

sources.notes: CONFIRMED at STATE level from the responsible ministry (official regional body, not a university marketing page): Baden-Württemberg imposes a mandatory non-EU international tuition of EUR 1,500 per semester on its universities, in force since winter semester 2017/18. It is a LANDESGEBÜHR under the Landeshochschulgebührengesetz (LHGebG), i.e. state law, applicable to Bachelor, consecutive Master and Staatsexamen programmes. Unit is explicitly per semester. Who is affected: all students who are not nationals of an EU or EEA state (and 'future students' — so it does not apply retroactively to those already enrolled before the fee was introduced). GAP: the ministry page does not state the amount of the separate mandatory semester contribution (Semesterbeitrag); that figure is university-specific and is recorded separately per university below. The ministry page also does not quantify the 300 EUR/semester share retained by universities that appears in the German-language version of the same page family.

sources.notes: CONFIRMED from the primary federal statute (correct URL is /stag/__10.html, NOT /stag_1913/__10.html which 404s). Germany naturalisation, discretionary entitlement (Anspruchseinbürgerung) under § 10 StAG: minimum 5 YEARS of lawful habitual residence in Germany ('seit fünf Jahren rechtmäßig seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland'). This is the post-2024 figure; it was reduced from 8 years by the Gesetz zur Modernisierung des Staatsangehörigkeitsrechts of 22 March 2024 (in force 27 June 2024). CRITICAL POINT THAT MUST NOT BE MISSED IN THE CORPUS: § 10(1) no. 2 requires the applicant to hold an unlimited residence right, an EU Blue Card, or a residence permit for a purpose OTHER THAN those listed in §§ 16a, 16b, 16d, 16e, 16f, 17, 18f, 19, 19b, 19e, 20, 20a, 22, 23a, 24, 25(3)-(5) and § 104c AufenthG — and § 16b is the STUDY permit. So five years on a § 16b student residence permit do NOT by themselves satisfy the naturalisation route; the student must first hold a qualifying non-student title. Also confirmed: § 10(3) and § 10(3a) are now marked '(weggefallen)' (repealed) — the former 3-year reduced-residence route for special integration achievements no longer exists. Language: CEFR B1 (§ 10(4)); legal/social knowledge: usually via the Einbürgerungstest (§ 10(5)), with Einbürgerungskurse offered but attendance not mandatory. Additional: commitment to the free democratic order and to Germany's special historical responsibility; livelihood secured without SGB II/XII benefits; no disqualifying conviction.

sources.notes: CONFIRMED: the mandatory semester fee at TUM, stated as a CAMPUS-DEPENDENT amount and explicitly tied to summer semester 2026. EUR 97.00 at Munich/Garching/Weihenstephan and Heilbronn; EUR 82.00 at Straubing. This is the mandatory fee (StudentCard/semester contribution) payable by ALL students, separate from and additional to the non-EU tuition. Cross-reference: TUM's tuition page states 'The regular semester fee must be paid in addition to the tuition fees', so tuition and this fee are distinct and additive. IMPORTANT NUANCE FOR THE CORPUS: this is one university's own fee, NOT a German-wide figure. It must not be used as a national value. Unit is per semester; the page gives an explicit semester (summer semester 2026), so as_of is 2026.
